---
title: Subtitles and transcripts
description: Have ClipMux transcribe a video's speech into subtitles the player shows, and read the transcript as text with timings.
---

ClipMux can transcribe a video's speech into a subtitles track. The player
shows it in its captions menu with no extra code, any HLS player finds it in
the playlist, and your backend can read the same transcript as text, with
segment and word timings, for search, notes or an AI feature of your own.

Transcription runs where the server's owner set it up: on the server's own
workers with [whisper.cpp](/docs/self-host/captions-and-ai/whisper), or with
a [speech API](/docs/self-host/captions-and-ai/speech-apis) they connected.
Your app asks for subtitles the same way in both cases.

<LeavesYourServers>
  If the owner connected a speech API, the video's audio is sent to that
  provider to be transcribed. With whisper.cpp, nothing leaves the
  owner's machines.
</LeavesYourServers>

## Before you start

- An API key with `assets:write` to ask for subtitles, and `assets:read` to
  read tracks and transcripts. The default scopes have both.
- A video with speech in it. ClipMux detects the language.

## Ask for subtitles [#ask-for-subtitles]

### At upload

Add `generate` when you create the upload:

```ts title="app/api/clipmux/[action]/route.ts"
async upload(req, { file }) {
  return { passthrough: 'lesson_42', title: file.name, generate: { subtitles: true } }
},
```

`generate` works the same on `POST /v1/uploads`, on an import with
`POST /v1/assets`, and with the client's `uploads.create`.
`generate: { chapters: true }` asks for subtitles too, since chapters are
made from them.

Subtitles are made after the video is ready, and never hold it up:
`video.asset.ready` comes first, then the track's own event.

### For a video you already have

```ts
const { track, job } = await clipmux.tracks.create('ast_…', { kind: 'subtitles' })
// track: { id: 'trk_…', kind: 'subtitles', source: 'generated', status: 'preparing' }
```

`POST /v1/assets/{id}/tracks` with `{"kind": "subtitles"}` answers `202`.
If the video already has subtitles, a new track is made and the old one
keeps playing until the new one is ready. It refuses with `409` and:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `asset_not_ready` | The video is still processing. Wait for `video.asset.ready`. |
| `no_audio` | The video has no audio track. |
| `job_active` | Another job is changing this video. Wait, or send `"supersede": true` to cancel a transcription that's running. |
| `asset_deleted` | The video is deleted. |

## Know when it's ready

A track's `status` is `preparing`, `ready` or `errored`. It's on the video,
in `tracks`, and ClipMux sends a webhook when it changes:

| Event | When |
| --- | --- |
| `video.asset.track.ready` | The track is ready to play and read. |
| `video.asset.track.errored` | Transcription failed. `track.error_code` says why. |
| `video.asset.track.deleted` | The track was deleted. |

Track events carry `track: {id, kind, error_code?}` beside the video. With
`clipmuxHandler`, your `asset` callback gets the video with its current
`tracks`, and the event as its second argument:

```ts
async asset(asset, event) {
  const subtitles = asset.tracks?.find((t) => t.kind === 'subtitles' && t.status === 'ready')
  await db.lesson.update({ where: { ref: asset.passthrough }, data: { subtitlesTrackId: subtitles?.id } })
},
```

See [Receive webhooks](/docs/build/webhooks).

## Show them

`<clipmux-player>` needs nothing more: a ready subtitles track is listed in
the video's HLS playlist, so it appears in the player's captions menu,
labelled with its language. Other HLS players find it in the same place.

For a player that wants a WebVTT file, the track is also at:

```txt
https://media.example.com/v/{token}/{playback_id}/tracks/{track_id}.vtt
```

or under `/p/{playback_id}/…` for a public playback ID.

## Read the transcript

```ts
const t = await clipmux.tracks.transcript('ast_…', 'trk_…')
```

`GET /v1/assets/{id}/tracks/{track_id}/transcript` returns, the moment the
track reads `ready`:

```json
{
  "track_id": "trk_…",
  "language": "en",
  "duration_ms": 612400,
  "text": "Welcome to the course. Today we…",
  "segments": [{ "id": "s0", "start_ms": 0, "end_ms": 4200, "text": "Welcome to the course." }]
}
```

Times are in milliseconds. `language` is the detected language code, for
example `en` or `hi`. Add `words: true` (`?words=true`) for each segment's
word timings. Before the track is ready, the route answers
`409 track_not_ready`.

If you store the text in Postgres, strip any `\u0000` characters first:
Postgres `text` columns refuse them.

## Remove subtitles

```ts
await clipmux.tracks.delete('ast_…', 'trk_…')
```

`DELETE /v1/assets/{id}/tracks/{track_id}` removes the track. Its file and
transcript go at once; it answers `202` while the track is taken out of the
playlist and `200` once nothing lists it.

## When transcription fails

An `errored` track's `error_code` is one of:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `no_audio` | The video has no audio. |
| `transcribe_failed` | Speech recognition failed. |
| `transcribe_unavailable` | No worker or speech API can transcribe right now. |
| `transcript_invalid` | The transcript that came back was not valid. |
| `speech_api_rejected` | The speech API refused the request. The server's owner should check its key and model. |
| `speech_api_unavailable` | The speech API kept failing. |

To try again, ask for subtitles with `POST /v1/assets/{id}/tracks`.

## What it doesn't do

- One language per video, detected from the speech. There is no language
  hint, and no translation.
- No uploading your own caption files.
- No editing a transcript.

## Check it works

Upload a short clip with speech and `generate: { subtitles: true }`, or run
`tracks.create` on a ready video. Your webhook receives
`video.asset.track.ready` once it's transcribed. Then:

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/v1/assets/ast_…/tracks/trk_…/transcript \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" | head -c 300
```

prints the transcript, and the player's captions button lists the language.
